294	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
295	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
296	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
297	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
298	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
299	why they are bundled.
300	
301	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
302	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
303	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
304	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
305	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
306	labelled as strictly weaker.
307	
308	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
309	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
310	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
311	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
312	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
313	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
314	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
315	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
316	
317	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
318	The project reaches this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single
319	named `sorry` that the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with
320	a weaker conditional statement to make a count go down.
321

323	previous text named the inputs of a route this project does not take.** That
324	text said the inputs are `Div` representability "which needs the Quot scheme"
325	(Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`) together with the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma
326	`smoothProperQuotient`. Both belong to the **Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient
327	route**, which is `rejected` on the board (`AJC.picrep.quot`,
328	`AJC.picrep.serre`) — so a reader who trusted this docstring concluded, wrongly,
329	that the seam's own inputs had been abandoned.

332	alternative D3), and it needs neither:

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

10	
11	/-!
12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302), and a
44	representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology. So an
45	unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a **false** statement, not
46	merely an unproved one. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
47	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
48	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
49	
50	```
51	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
52	```
53	
54	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
55	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
56	both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
57	the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
58	of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
59	declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
60	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
61	`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)
62	
63	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
64	
65	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
66	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
67	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
68	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
69	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
70	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
71	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
72	
73	## Main results
74	
75	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
76	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
77	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
78	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
79	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
80	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
81	* `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` —
82	  the **conditional** Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the
83	  challenge, not the headline.
84	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
85	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
86	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
87	  quotient encoding).
88	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
89	  scheme and the natural bijection
90	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
91	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
92	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
93	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
94	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
95	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
96	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
97	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
98	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
99	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
100	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
101	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
102	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
103	
104	## Remaining obligations
105	
106	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
107	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
108	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
109	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
110	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
111	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**. Its inputs are the
112	Milne–Kollár ones — `Div^d` through the Grassmannian and a finite Galois
113	quotient — *not* Quot and *not* `smoothProperQuotient`; see the "Which route
114	discharges it" paragraph on `fgaPicardRepresentability` below, which corrects an
115	earlier claim here that the inputs were blocked on Quot. Everything else here — the representing scheme,
116	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
117	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
118	that one existence statement.
119	
120	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
121	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
122	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
123	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
124	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
125	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
126	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
127	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
128	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
129	
130	## References
131	
132	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
133	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
134	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
135	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
136	-/

147	
148	/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
149	section `σ : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
150	curves of this project this is the pointing `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ C`
151	already threaded through the Albanese statements (`AlgebraicJacobian.IsAlbanese`).
152	
153	This is the hypothesis of Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: together with

242	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes; the

247	/-- Typeclass asserting existence of a scheme over `Spec k` that represents

252	producer is `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, which needs `[HasRationalPoint C]`

255	there is deliberately **no instance**: without a section the plain relative

273	  has_pic_scheme : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),

285	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
286	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
287	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
288	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
289	  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose
290	
291	/-- **THE PROJECT'S CENTRAL OPEN OBLIGATION — expected to stay open.**
292	
293	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch`: for a smooth proper geometrically
294	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
295	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
296	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
297	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
298	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
299	why they are bundled.
300	
301	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
302	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
303	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
304	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
305	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
306	labelled as strictly weaker.
307	
308	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
309	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
310	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
311	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
312	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
313	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
314	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
315	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
316	
317	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
318	The project reaches this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single
319	named `sorry` that the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with
320	a weaker conditional statement to make a count go down.
321	
322	**Which route discharges it — corrected 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), because the
323	previous text named the inputs of a route this project does not take.** That
324	text said the inputs are `Div` representability "which needs the Quot scheme"
325	(Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`) together with the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma
326	`smoothProperQuotient`. Both belong to the **Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient
327	route**, which is `rejected` on the board (`AJC.picrep.quot`,
328	`AJC.picrep.serre`) — so a reader who trusted this docstring concluded, wrongly,
329	that the seam's own inputs had been abandoned.
330	
331	The committed route is **Milne–Kollár** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`,
332	alternative D3), and it needs neither:
333	
334	* `Div^d` representability comes through the **Grassmannian**, not Quot:
335	  degree slices of `Scheme.DivFunctor` (`Picard/DivDegree.lean`, landed), an
336	  embedding into `Scheme.Grassmannian` of the section module, locally closed
337	  carving, and `Grassmannian.representable`
338	  (`Picard/GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`, proved) — campaign milestones
339	  D1′–D4′. D4′ also delivers the locally closed immersion into `Gr` that serves
340	  as the quasi-projectivity certificate.
341	* the quotient is the **finite Galois** quotient of a semilinear action whose
342	  finite orbits lie in affine opens — campaign G2, in
343	  `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` (`sorry`-free) with Speiser descent under
344	  `Picard/GaloisDescent/`. It is *not* `smoothProperQuotient`, which is false as
345	  stated in Lean (see the §4 note below) and must not be built against.
346	  **`sorry`-free is not gate-free here**: the affine case is proved
347	  (`isGaloisQuotientSpec`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine.lean`) and the
348	  gluing substrate exists, but the general existence statement is still the
349	  instance-free class `HasGaloisQuotient` (`FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`), whose
350	  only producer is a single-field non-vacuity witness
351	  (`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean`). So G2 is *substantially* built, not
352	  discharged.
353	
354	What remains is those campaign modules — uniform `H¹` vanishing (P5, the open
355	`AJC.rr.extuniform` leaf), the `picSharp` Zariski-sheaf/degree/separatedness
356	devices (B1, B4, B6), the `Div^d` chain (D2′–D4′), the Milne glue over a
357	separably closed field (J1–J5, which also needs a universe bridge since
358	`picSharp` is `Type (u+1)`-valued while Mathlib's 01JJ engine wants `Type u`),
359	Galois descent of `picSharp` points (G3), and the coproduct assembly (G4) —
360	**plus one further item that no campaign milestone covers**, recorded next.
361	
362	**THE ELEVENTH ITEM, and it is unowned: every campaign milestone targets
363	`picSharp`, while clause (1) above is about `picEt`.** The campaign
364	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`) was written on 2026-07-09 for the
365	`picSharp`-shaped obligation, before the étale decision of 2026-07-28
366	(protection `I-0491`). Its J-cluster represents `picSharpDeg C' r`, G3 descends
367	`picSharp` points, and G4 assembles `picSharpDeg`; the word `picEt` does not
368	occur in any milestone body. So completing all of them yields representability
369	of `picSharp`, **not** of `picEt`, and the gap cannot be closed by composing with
370	`picEtComparison`: that comparison is an isomorphism only under a section
371	(Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5, clause (2) of this very statement), and a section is exactly
372	the hypothesis `I-0491` forbids the headline to carry. The paragraph above on
373	sheafification says why this is not a technicality — an unconditional
374	`RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be FALSE, so the campaign's endpoint
375	cannot be transported to clause (1) for free. Representability of the sheafified
376	functor itself is therefore a genuine additional obligation, which the campaign
377	names as outstanding in its own preamble but never schedules. The board node
378	`AJC.picrep` carries the current landed/absent split and this item.
379	
380	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
381	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
382	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison theorem
383	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and the conditional
384	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from it.
385	
386	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
387	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
388	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
389	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
390	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
391	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
392	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
393	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
394	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
395	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
396	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
397	than asserting it. -/
398	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability {k : Type u} [Field k]
399	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
400	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
401	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
402	    (∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
403	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
404	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
405	      ∧ (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
406	  sorry
407	
408	/-- **The étale representability gate**, as a `Prop`-class so that consumers can
409	quantify over it as a hypothesis and stay kernel-clean.
410	
411	Unlike the legacy `HasPicScheme`, this class carries **no** hypothesis on
412	`C(k)`: its unique producer `instHasPicSchemeEt` is unconditional. It is the
413	carrier of the project's central open obligation. -/
414	class HasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
415	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
416	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
417	  has_pic_scheme_et : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
418	    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
419	      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom
420	
421	/-- The étale gate fires for **every** smooth proper geometrically integral
422	curve, with no rational-point hypothesis — which is the whole content of the
423	owner decision of 2026-07-28. Its mathematics is
424	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, the one open obligation. -/
425	instance instHasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
426	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
427	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
428	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasPicSchemeEt C :=
429	  ⟨(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1⟩
430	
431	/-- **The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the scheme
432	representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
433	
434	This is the honest `Pic_{C/k}` of the project — available for every smooth
435	proper geometrically integral curve, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`. The legacy
436	`PicScheme` (representing the unsheafified `picSharp`) exists only under a
437	rational point and is retained for the consumers written against it. -/
438	noncomputable def PicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
439	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
440	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
441	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
442	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
443	  (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose
444	
445	/-- **Representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` by `Pic_{C/k}`, over an arbitrary
446	field**: the natural bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)`.
447	
448	The étale-formulation replacement for `PicScheme.representable`. Consumers of
449	the tangent-space chain should compose with *this* `homEquiv`; the `picSharp`
450	version is available only under `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/

573	/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence
574	
575	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
576	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
577	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
578	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
579	
580	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
581	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
582	
583	/-! ### The Abel map
584	
585	The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
586	`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
587	supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.
588	
589	Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
590	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
591	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
592	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
593	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
594	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
595	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
596	negation on the group-valued functor.
597	
598	Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
599	`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
600	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism
601	under the divisor conditions (`Modules.isIso_pullbackKernelComparison`, whose
602	side hypotheses — epi `q`, quasi-coherent source, finitely-presented `F`,
603	`T`-flat `F`, invertible kernel — are exactly the fields of `DivFamily`), so
604	`ker` commutes with base change and the class `[ker q]` is natural.  Negation
605	is natural because `Pic^♯`'s pullback maps are group homomorphisms.
606	
607	The `dual` route (`Modules.dual (ker q)` as an explicit inverse) is available
608	for the *object-level* invertibility (`dual_isLocallyTrivial`) but is not used
609	here: the group-inverse `-[ker q]` is the canonical `[I_D⁻¹]` and makes
610	naturality rest only on the kernel–pullback comparison, avoiding the
611	not-yet-formalised sheaf-level dual-pullback commutation.
612	
613	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
614	Def. `dfn:Abel`); this instance is the **natural-transformation half** — `Div`
615	representability (Kleiman §3 Thm. `th:repDiv`) is NOT claimed here. -/

618	divisor equivalence relation `DivFamily.Rel`: an equivalence `f : x.F ≅ y.F`

620	iso `f.hom`), hence equal `H_T`-coset classes (`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/

>      true, it is strictly weaker than the challenge, and protection `I-0491` clause 4
>      forbids presenting it as the headline;
>    - the étale-sheafified functor itself is **built and `sorry`-free**
>      (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`, sheaf property *proved*), so the remaining distance
>      from these milestones to the headline is the comparison
>      `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` — which is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 and is available
>      only under a section — plus representability of the sheafified functor itself.
>      Both are bundled into the single obligation `fgaPicardRepresentability`, so
>      that count stays honest in both directions.
>
>    **Two things established while the question was open, which survive it.** Both
>    are about the milestones' hypothesis bundle rather than about the decision, so
>    they are still load-bearing.
>
>    - `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`, which every milestone below assumes, is
>      **free** given the challenge hypotheses: a smooth morphism is geometrically
>      reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, proved in mathlib generality at

>      which runs over a separably closed field where rational points are cheap.
> 2. *Cluster P's provenance.* Cluster P (χ-ledger, section drops, uniform `H¹`
>    vanishing) is the longest pole, and the sibling
>    `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` carries a large sorry-free
>    `RiemannRoch/` development covering much of it. Whether each statement is

**G4 — Coproduct assembly.**
(i) `X := ∐_{d:ℤ} X_d`, each `X_d` := copy of `J_r` relabelled through A1's translation `picSharpDeg d ≅ picSharpDeg r`. Mathlib verified: `HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete σ) Scheme.{u}` + `CoproductsOfShapeDisjoint` + disjoint `Sigma.ι` open covers (`AlgebraicGeometry/Limits.lean:187-225`); `LocallyOfFiniteType` along `Sigma.desc` via `sigmaDesc` (`Morphisms/Basic.lean:303`, verified) + FT-descent along `Spec k' → Spec k` (D2-M13: `k'⊗_k A₀` FT ⟹ A₀ FT). New bricks: `hom_sigma_decompose` (T-map = clopen partition + components, matched to B4), `isSeparated_sigma` (verified absent from mathlib; provable via `IsZariskiLocalAtTarget` + disjoint cover).

**H0 — Hygiene (anytime).** Fix stale docstrings (`QuotFunctorDef.lean:456`, `DivFunctorDef.lean:76-79`, `QuotScheme.lean:230/:301`, `IdentityComponent.lean:262`); note `HasDivFunctor` vacuity (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean:185`); repin `PicScheme.degree` (`IdentityComponent.lean:1452`) through B4's `picSharpDeg`; docstring-flag `HasSmoothProperQuotient` (:541) as permanently off-path.

**Edges (summary):** G5←{G3,G4}; G4←{A1,B4,G2,G3}; G3←{B0,B1,G1,G2}; G1←{J5,B2}; J5←{J3,J4,B1,B6}; J4←{P4,P5,B5}; J3←{J2,B1,B2,B3}; J2←{B3,J1,A2,D4'}; J1←{D4',B5,P3}; D4'←{D1',D2',D3'}; D3'←{B3}; D2'←{P5,B3,P3}; D1'←∅; A2←{D1',B4}; A1←{B4}; B6←{B3,B5,P3,P4,B0}; B5←{B3}; B4←{B2,B3,P3}; B3←{P1,P2,P3}; B2←∅; B1←{B0}; B0←∅; P5←{P2,P3,P4}; P4←{P2,P3}; P3←{P2}; P2←{P1}; P1←∅; G2←∅.

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	
9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71	
72	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
74	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
75	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
76	-/
77	
78	set_option autoImplicit false
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory
83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
85	
86	namespace Scheme
87	
88	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
89	
90	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
91	
92	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
93	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
94	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
95	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
96	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
97	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
98	
99	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
100	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
101	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
102	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
103	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
104	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
105	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
106	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
107	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
108	
109	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
110	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
111	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
112	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
113	sieve on the underlying scheme.
114	
115	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
116	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
117	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
118	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
119	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
120	  intro T S hS
121	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
122	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
123	
124	namespace PicSharp
125	
126	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
127	
128	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
129	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
130	
131	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
132	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
133	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
134	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
135	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
136	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
137	
138	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
139	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
140	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
141	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
142	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
143	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
144	
145	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
146	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
147	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
148	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
149	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
150	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
151	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
152	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
153	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
154	
155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property
170	
171	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
178	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
189	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
190	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
194	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
195	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
196	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
197	
198	end PicSharp
199	
200	namespace PicScheme
201	
202	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
203	
204	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
205	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
206	forgotten,
207	
208	```
209	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
210	```
211	
212	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
213	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
214	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
215	`picSharp`.
216	
217	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
218	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
219	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
220	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
221	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
222	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
223	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
224	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
225	
226	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
227	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
228	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
229	
230	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
231	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
232	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
233	the name is not available here). -/
234	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
235	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
238	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
239	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
240	
241	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
242	
243	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
244	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
245	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
246	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
247	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
248	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
249	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
250	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
251	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
252	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
253	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
254	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
255	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
256	  exact h
257	
258	end PicScheme
259	
260	end Scheme
261	
262	end AlgebraicGeometry

import Mathlib

/-!
# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor

This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).

## Why the sheafification is the right object

The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
hypothesis.

There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
supplied:

1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).

## The site

Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
hypothesis.

## Main definitions

* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
  relative Picard presheaf.
* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
  must match.

## References

Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.

=== sheaf thm:
The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
the name is not available here). -/
noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})

/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**

The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
  exact h

end PicScheme

145	/-! ## Semilinear Galois actions on schemes over `Spec L` -/
146	
147	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
148	
149	/-- A **semilinear `Gal(L/K)`-action** on a scheme `X` over `Spec L` (campaign
150	`G2(a)`): a group homomorphism into scheme automorphisms of the total space, each
151	automorphism lying in a commuting square over the corresponding Galois automorphism
152	`Spec γ` of the base.  (`X` is *not* acted on over `Spec L` — only the composite
153	descends to `Spec K`; this is exactly Kleiman/Milne's "descent datum" for the finite
154	Galois cover `Spec L → Spec K`.) -/
155	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
156	  /-- The action by scheme automorphisms. -/
157	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
158	  /-- Each automorphism covers the Galois action `Spec γ` on the base. -/
159	  compat (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
160	    (act γ).hom ≫ f = f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom
161	
162	namespace SemilinearGalAction
163	
164	variable {K L}
165	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
166	
167	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between two semilinearly-acted schemes over `Spec L`. -/
168	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
169	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (ρ' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f')
170	    (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
171	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (ρ'.act γ).hom
172	
173	/-- The `Γ`-orbit of a point of `X` under a semilinear action. -/
174	def orbit (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
175	  Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x
176	
177	/-- **Orbit-in-affine hypothesis** (campaign `G2`, audit item 8): every `Γ`-orbit is
178	contained in an affine open.  This hypothesis is **essential** (Hironaka trap — see
179	the module docstring): without it the quotient exists only as an algebraic space.
180	For finite Galois `L/K` every orbit is finite, so this is the standard EGA II 4.5.4
181	hypothesis; it holds e.g. for quasi-projective `X` (finite point sets of
182	quasi-projective schemes lie in affine opens) and is supplied to the campaign
183	consumer by the Γ-stable `V_Σ` covers of `J5`. -/
184	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
185	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
186	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom.base x ∈ U.1
187	
188	/-- A `Γ`-stable open of `X`. -/
189	def IsStableOpen (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
190	  ∀ γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (ρ.act γ).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
191	
192	end SemilinearGalAction

194	/-- GATE (campaign `G2(a)`, EGA II 4.5.4 pattern; `Prop`-class, **no instances** — do
195	not instantiate except by proving the geometry).  A `Γ`-stable affine refinement:
196	every point admits a `Γ`-stable affine open neighbourhood.  The intended discharge:
197	from `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, given an orbit inside affine `U`, prime avoidance produces
198	`s ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪)` with the orbit inside `D(s) ⊆ ⋂_γ γU`, and the product `∏_γ γ(s)` cuts
199	out a `Γ`-stable affine basic open — a genuine multi-session lemma (walls: transport
200	of sections along the action isomorphisms, and basic-open-affineness bookkeeping),
201	pinned here per the campaign plan ("may be pinned as a separate gated statement if it
202	walls"). -/
203	class HasStableAffineCover {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
204	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
205	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
206	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ ρ.IsStableOpen U

233	section PullbackAction

235	/-- Each Galois automorphism of `Spec L` is a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
236	lemma toSpecAut_hom_comp_baseMap (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
237	    (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))
238	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) := by
239	  rw [toSpecAut_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
240	  congr 2
241	  ext x
242	  exact AlgEquiv.commutes γ⁻¹ x

244	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
245	
246	/-- The single automorphism of the base change `Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L` induced by
247	`γ` through the second factor. -/
248	noncomputable abbrev pullbackGalMap (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
249	    pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
250	      ⟶ pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) :=
251	  pullback.map g _ g _ (𝟙 Y) (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom (𝟙 _)
252	    (by simp) (by rw [Category.comp_id, toSpecAut_hom_comp_baseMap])
253

255	lemma pullbackGalMap_fst (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
256	    pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
257	      = pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) := by
258	  have h : pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
259	      = pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫ 𝟙 Y :=
260	    pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
261	  rw [h, Category.comp_id]

263	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
264	lemma pullbackGalMap_snd (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
265	    pullbackGalMap K L g γ ≫ pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
266	      = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫
267	          (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L γ).hom :=
268	  pullback.lift_snd _ _ _
269	
270	/-- The canonical semilinear Galois action on a base change
271	`Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L → Spec L` through the second factor.  This is the reference
272	action used to *state* equivariance of descent isomorphisms and the `T`-points
273	property. -/
274	noncomputable def pullbackSemilinearGalAction :
275	    SemilinearGalAction K L
276	      (pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))))
277	      (pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))) where
278	  act := MonoidHom.mk'
279	    (fun γ =>
280	      { hom := pullbackGalMap K L g γ
281	        inv := pullbackGalMap K L g γ⁻¹
282	        hom_inv_id := by
283	          apply pullback.hom_ext
284	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, Category.id_comp]
285	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc,
286	              toSpecAut_hom_inv_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
287	        inv_hom_id := by
288	          apply pullback.hom_ext
289	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, Category.id_comp]
290	          · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc,
291	              toSpecAut_inv_hom_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp] })
292	    (fun γ τ => by
293	      refine Iso.ext ?_
294	      change pullbackGalMap K L g (γ * τ)
295	        = pullbackGalMap K L g τ ≫ pullbackGalMap K L g γ
296	      apply pullback.hom_ext
297	      · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst, pullbackGalMap_fst]
298	      · rw [Category.assoc, pullbackGalMap_snd, pullbackGalMap_snd,
299	          pullbackGalMap_snd_assoc, toSpecAut_mul_hom])
300	  compat γ := pullback.lift_snd _ _ _

303	    ((pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).act γ).hom = pullbackGalMap K L g γ := rfl

307	/-- The base change to `Spec L` of a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
308	noncomputable abbrev pullbackBaseChange (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
309	    pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
310	      ⟶ pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) :=
311	  pullback.map t _ g _ u (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by rw [Category.comp_id, hu]) (by simp)

315	    pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫

317	      = pullback.fst t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≫ u :=

323	        pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))

326	        pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))

333	/-- Naturality of the base-change action: base changes of morphisms over `Spec K`
334	are equivariant for the canonical actions. -/
335	lemma pullbackGalMap_naturality (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
336	    pullbackGalMap K L t γ ≫ pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu
337	      = pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫ pullbackGalMap K L g γ := by

340	/-- The base change of a morphism over `Spec K`, composed with an equivariant
341	morphism, is equivariant.  (The "easy direction" of the `T`-points property of a
342	Galois quotient: descended morphisms induce equivariant ones.) -/
343	theorem SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
344	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
345	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
346	    {e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X}
347	    (he : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant ρ e)
348	    (u : T ⟶ Y) (hu : u ≫ g = t) :
349	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant ρ
350	      (pullbackBaseChange K L g t u hu ≫ e) := by
351	  intro γ
352	  rw [pullbackSemilinearGalAction_act_hom, ← Category.assoc,
353	    pullbackGalMap_naturality g t u hu γ, Category.assoc, Category.assoc]

360	section Quotient
361	
362	variable {K L}
363	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
364	
365	/-- `(Y, g)` is a **finite Galois quotient** of the semilinearly-acted `(X, f, ρ)`
366	(campaign `G2`): there is an isomorphism `e : Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L ≅ X` which is
367	
368	1. over `Spec L`,
369	2. `Γ`-equivariant for the canonical base-change action, and
370	3. universal: every equivariant morphism `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L ⟶ X` over `Spec L`
371	   descends **uniquely** to `T ⟶ Y` over `Spec K` — this clause is exactly
372	   `Hom_K(T, Y) ≅ Hom_L(T_L, X)^Γ` (the inverse bijection direction is
373	   `SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackMap_comp`). -/
374	def IsGaloisQuotient (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
375	    (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : Prop :=
376	  ∃ e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≅ X,
377	    e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ∧
378	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant ρ e.hom ∧
379	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
380	      (h : pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X),
381	      h ≫ f = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) →
382	      (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant ρ h →
383	      ∃! u : {u : T ⟶ Y // u ≫ g = t},
384	        pullbackBaseChange K L g t u.1 u.2 ≫ e.hom = h

606	/-! ## §6. The local-constancy gate (relative-curve regime) -/
607	
608	/-- **Gate: divisor families on the curve have locally constant fibre degree**
609	(instance-free Prop-class, house `HasPicScheme` pattern — the deep heart is
610	deferred, never sorried).
611	
612	Mathematical content (TRUE at this pinned generality; Mumford, *Abelian
613	Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`): for a smooth proper relative
614	curve `C/k` and any `T`, a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` is finite
615	flat over `T` (proper + quasi-finite: each `D_t` is the zero scheme of a
616	regular section of an invertible ideal on the curve `C_t`, hence
617	`0`-dimensional), so `q_* O_D` is finite locally free and its fibre rank —
618	`DivFamily.fiberDeg` — is Zariski-locally constant.  Discharge route: the
619	finiteness/rank half of the campaign's B3 rigid-pushforward engine plus
620	relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness; both are outside the current in-tree
621	substrate, hence the gate.

/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence

The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.

Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/

/-! ### The Abel map

The class `HasAbelMap` carries the map itself (a data field `abel`), so that
`abelMap` has the defining property `abelMap_app_mk` below; the instance
supplies the explicit natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`.

Construction of `abelMapWitness C : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)]`:
a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
negation on the group-valued functor.

Naturality of `abelKernelNatTrans` is the mathematical heart: for a test map
`g : T' ⟶ T` the base-change square is cartesian (`quotBaseSquare`), and the
**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism

import re, sys, json
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/picaudit')
from strip import strip_comments

DECL = re.compile(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+|unsafe\s+|partial\s+|scoped\s+|local\s+)*'
                  r'(theorem|lemma|def|instance|abbrev|class|structure|example|axiom|opaque)\b')

def decls(path):
    src = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    code = strip_comments(src)
    lines = code.split('\n')
    # find declaration start lines (column 0-ish, top-level)
    starts = []
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        if DECL.match(l):
            starts.append(i)
        elif re.match(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+|unsafe\s+)*$', l) and l.strip():
            # attribute-only / modifier-only line: check next line
            pass
    out = []
    for idx, s in enumerate(starts):
        e = starts[idx+1] if idx+1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        # trim: declaration body ends at next top-level non-indented construct
        body = lines[s:e]
        # signature = up to and including the line containing ':=' or 'where' or the
        # first line whose indentation returns to 0 after the header (proof body)
        sig_end = len(body)
        for j, l in enumerate(body):
            if j > 0 and l and not l[0].isspace() and not l.strip().startswith(('|','⟨')):
                sig_end = j; break
        sig_region = body[:sig_end]
        # binder region: everything before ':=' (term) ; for theorems the type IS part of sig
        joined = '\n'.join(sig_region)
        m = DECL.match(body[0])
        kind = m.group(1)
        nm = re.sub(r'^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*', '', body[0])
        nm = re.sub(r'^(?:private\s+|protected\s+|noncomputable\s+|unsafe\s+|partial\s+|scoped\s+|local\s+)*', '', nm)
        nm = nm.split(None, 2)
        name = nm[1] if len(nm) > 1 else '?'
        name = name.rstrip(':')
        out.append(dict(file=path, line=s+1, kind=kind, name=name, sig=joined))
    return out

if __name__ == '__main__':
    which = sys.argv[1]   # 'plain' | 'et'
    allres = []
    for p in sys.argv[2:]:
        for d in decls(p):
            sig = d['sig']
            # split off proof body at ':=' at top level to avoid counting proof-term mentions
            # binder occurrences: '[' ... 'HasPicScheme' ... ']'
            hits_plain = re.findall(r'\[[^\[\]]*\bHasPicScheme\b[^\[\]]*\]', sig)
            hits_et    = re.findall(r'\[[^\[\]]*\bHasPicSchemeEt\b[^\[\]]*\]', sig)
            hits_plain = [h for h in hits_plain if 'HasPicSchemeEt' not in h]
            tgt = hits_plain if which=='plain' else hits_et
            if tgt:
                allres.append((d['file'], d['line'], d['kind'], d['name'], len(tgt), hits_plain and 1 or 0, hits_et and 1 or 0))
    for r in allres:
        print(f"{r[0]}:{r[1]}\t{r[2]}\t{r[3]}\tbinders={r[4]}\tplain={r[5]}\tet={r[6]}")
    print(f"TOTAL_DECLS={len(allres)}")
PYEOF
FILES=$(grep -rl "HasPicScheme" --include=*.lean .)
echo "########## PLAIN HasPicScheme binder declarations ##########"
python3 /tmp/picaudit/decls.py plain $FILES
echo
echo "########## HasPicSchemeEt binder declarations ##########"
python3 /tmp/picaudit/decls.py et $FILES
